items.summary: PARIS — France test-fired an upgraded version of its M51 strategic ballistic missile from a submarine for the first time on Tuesday, a capability demonstration that President Emmanuel Macron called “very important” for the country’s strategic credibility and which he said would be monitored by allies and adversaries alike. evidenceRecords.text: PARIS — France test-fired an upgraded version of its M51 strategic ballistic missile from a submarine for the first time on Tuesday, a capability demonstration that President Emmanuel Macron called “very important” for the country’s strategic credibility and which he said would be monitored by allies and adversaries alike.

Today’s launch was the seventh time a variant of the M51 was fired from a French submarine, and the 13th launch of the missile overall, all of them “of course, conducted without a nuclear warhead,” according to the ministry.
The nuclear-powered ballistic-missile submarine Le Vigilant fired an M51.3 missile in an acceptance test following the boat’s overhaul, the Ministry of the Armed Forces said in a statement.

The missile, which didn’t carry a nuclear warhead, was launched off Finistère in western France and splashed down in the North Atlantic several hundred kilometers from any coastline, the ministry said.
The first version of the M51 was fired from the Biscarrosse launch site in 2006, with the first submarine launch from the SSBN Le Terrible in January 2010.

The company also confirmed that the ongoing contract for two Scorpène Evolved submarines already includes the capability to launch the SM39, as Naval News previously reported .
MBDA said it is offering the SM39 rather than the next-generation SM40 , which remains under development, because of Indonesia’s submarine production timeline.

The first and second Indonesian Scorpène Evolved submarines are scheduled for delivery in 2032 and 2033 , respectively, and MBDA wants to ensure that the Indonesian Navy (TNI AL) can equip the boats with a submarine-launched anti-ship missile at or soon after delivery if required.
The company said only minimal adjustments would be needed to use the newer missile, as the SM39 and SM40 use the same storage and launch capsule and both fit standard 533 mm submarine torpedo tubes.
MBDA expects Indonesia to formally order SM39 in early 2027.

About the SM39 Block 2 Mod 2 The SM39 launches from a torpedo tube inside a watertight capsule that carries the missile to the surface before releasing it for low-altitude, sea-skimming, high-subsonic flight.

The Block 2 Mod 2 represents the latest production standard of the SM39, incorporating updated electronics, improved seeker performance, and better electronic counter-countermeasure capability than earlier versions.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Xanadu and GlobalFoundries have entered a multi-year partnership to develop and manufacture photonic components for utility-scale quantum computing.
The companies plan to use the manufacturing platform for future photonic quantum modules and Xanadu ’s fault-tolerant quantum computing demonstrators.

PRESS RELEASE — Xanadu Quantum Technologies Limited (“ Xanadu “; NASDAQ/TSX: XNDU), a leading photonic quantum computing company, today announced a strategic multi-year partnership with GlobalFoundries (GF), a leading semiconductor manufacturer, to address the high-volume production required for utility-scale quantum computing.

This partnership combines Xanadu’s existing expertise in ultra-low loss photonic design and process development with GF’s industry-leading photonics manufacturing prowess to accelerate the development and manufacturing of advanced photonic components, including ultra-low loss silicon nitride (SiN) photonics and Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors (SNSPDs), through GF’s 300 mm production line in Malta, New York.

The adoption of SNSPDs is expected to dramatically increase the speed of Xanadu’s quantum computing systems and considerably reduce the chip overheads needed to deliver utility-scale quantum computers with Xanadu’s photonic quantum computing architecture.

Combining ultra-high efficiency SNSPDs with ultra-low loss SiN photonics, used as optical circuit boards to guide photons with negligible signal loss across a wide spectrum of light, forms the backbone of Xanadu’s photonic quantum computing technology.

In addition to SNSPDs and SiN, Xanadu and GF are exploring future work packages to further develop high-performance quantum modules that are intended to increase the power and utility of photonic quantum computing systems.

The output of this collaboration is expected to serve as the manufacturing foundation for Xanadu’s upcoming fault-tolerant demonstrators, supporting the company’s long-term objective of providing the hardware architecture for future quantum data centers.
“Transitioning quantum computing technology to a high-volume manufacturing line is fundamental to delivering quantum computing at scale,” said Dr.
Christian Weedbrook, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Xanadu .

“Partnering with GlobalFoundries allows Xanadu to refine and scale up our existing industry-leading photonics platform and apply GF’s industrial expertise and technology to our photonic chip production.

This partnership demonstrates our focus on execution and seeks to provide the reliable, precision-manufactured infrastructure necessary to transition quantum technology from the research environment to commercial-scale data centers.” “By combining Xanadu ’s advanced photonic computing technology with GF’s 300 mm manufacturing expertise, this partnership creates a path to industrialize the critical components needed to accelerate the deployment of fault-tolerant systems and enable future quantum computing architectures,” said Nicholas Sergeant, VP of Quantum Technology Solutions at GF.

PRESS RELEASE — Zapata Quantum (OTCQB: ZPTA) (“ Zapata ” or the “Company”) today announced it has joined the IBM Quantum Network with plans to use IBM’s world-class quantum computers with Zapata’s deep expertise in use-case discovery and application development.
The Company’s effort aims to help close the quantum application gap by translating advances in quantum computing into mission-critical applications and real-world impact.
“The rapid progress IBM is making on the path to fault-tolerant quantum computing brings the quantum application gap into sharper focus,” said Sumit Kapur, CEO of Zapata Quantum .

We are excited for Zapata’s Quantum Application Intelligence to translate organizations’ highest-mission priorities into practical quantum applications.” “ IBM ‘s roadmap to fault-tolerant quantum computing is one of the most credible in the industry, and superconducting qubits remain one of the most capable paths to advantage because their hardware is fast ,” said Jonny Olson, VP Strategy and Co-Founder of Zapata Quantum .

“Joining the IBM Quantum Network lets us better identify valuable opportunities for organizations that need the fastest systems, and then prepare those organizations for the precise moment that quantum gives them real ROI.” Joining the IBM Quantum Network builds on a history of joint IBM and Zapata research done on early quantum devices.

Zapata used IBM quantum computers in a landmark study published in Nature Biotechnology that produced experimentally validated candidates targeting KRAS and was selected as one of the journal’s Top 10 Articles of 2025.¹ Scientists from the two companies also co-authored research published in npj Quantum Information, which advanced the understanding of variational quantum factoring on a superconducting processor.
2 Being part of the IBM Quantum Network also reflects Zapata ’s broader strategy of working with technology leaders across the quantum and AI ecosystems.

Insights from being part of the IBM Quantum Network will inform Quantum Pilot , Zapata’s hardware-agnostic platform that helps enterprises identify, prioritize, and develop quantum applications as hardware matures.

items.originalTitle: Mirror Particle is building a ‘world model’ of human behavior
items.summary: Startups that promise to predict how humans will behave are having a moment. items.title: LibreOffice says ‘no AI’ is now a software feature
items.originalTitle: LibreOffice says ‘no AI’ is now a software feature
items.summary: If you’re looking for a document editor that doesn’t use artificial intelligence, LibreOffice may be just the software for you. The Document Foundation, the nonprofit software maker behind the open source document editor LibreOffice, said in a blog post this week that while it does not reject AI out of hand, it “will not add” AI to its software for the foreseeable future.

evidenceRecords.text: If you’re looking for a document editor that doesn’t use artificial intelligence, LibreOffice may be just the software for you.

The Document Foundation, the nonprofit software maker behind the open source document editor LibreOffice, said in a blog post this week that while it does not reject AI out of hand, it “will not add” AI to its software for the foreseeable future.
The blog post comes weeks after the release of the latest version of LibreOffice in late August, in which the nonprofit reiterated that the software “contains no generative AI features.”

LibreOffice said at the time that this was a “deliberate design position” to ensure that users’ documents are not uploaded to a server for processing and that no part of the software requires a network connection to function.
The nonprofit added that its software is used by tens of millions of people and organizations, and that users should retain control over their data.
LibreOffice says users can still choose to use AI tools by installing software extensions that connect the document editor to local AI models.

LibreOffice said that there is currently “no integration” that meets all of its requirements, such as ensuring that the users’ data stays on their device and that there is no reliance on a single AI provider, among other considerations.

The organization’s criteria for including AI into its software is not a “definitive rejection,” but the decision was an assessment of the technology today, rather than a “judgement on the value of the sector.”
LibreOffice is one of the many kinds of open source and alternative software used to escape the clutches of Silicon Valley tech giants.

WASHINGTON — Leonardo DRS has launched a new UK-based subsidiary known as DRS UK, which will begin locally producing tactical radios, the company announced Monday.
The release did say the new subsidiary will help support UK requirements for counter-drone capabilities, air defense and active protection systems.
It will also serve as a “strategic hub” for DRS’s tactical radio business more broadly across Europe.

“Establishing DRS UK and launching a full local tactical radar capability, strengthens our ability to support customers and partners with the proximity, responsiveness and manufacturing capacity needed to meet evolving operational requirements,” said Leonardo DRS CEO John Baylouny. “This investment enables closer collaboration with UK industry partners and integrators to deliver counter-UAS, air defence and force protection capabilities that help protect the warfighter.”
The new UK-based organization finds itself in a unique position as a European subsidiary of DRS, which itself is the American arm of the Italian defense giant Leonardo.

But when asked about the European market by Breaking Defense in an interview earlier this year, Baylouny said that Europe — like the United States — is seeking to acquire needed weaponry as soon as possible and has become somewhat agnostic on which country is providing the capability.

Progress in CFET integration is complemented with design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) studies that examine CFET device architectures from a circuit level perspective [2].
These studies aim to identify scalable standard cell configurations and performance boosters that offer the best tradeoff in terms of power, performance, area and cost.
In part 2, a scalable architecture for sCFET is introduced, allowing both split-gate and common-gate configurations.
Besides progressing the logic roadmap, DTCO work shows how this split-gate architecture also benefits CFET-based SRAM scaling.
Finally, improved back-end-of-line (BEOL) routability is demonstrated, supporting the scaling of CFET standard cells.

In various DTCO studies, imec has demonstrated the ability to scale CFET device architectures across subsequent logic technology nodes, supported by innovative standard cell configurations and scaling boosters.

evidenceRecords.text: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Beaver Brown Waters of… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search The Cree word pahtaaunaakun seems particularly apt for describing the distinctive brown hues of the waters that drain into Hannah Bay and Rupert

Meaning the “color of singed beaver” in Southern East Cree , the word evokes the rich brown of the humic-substance-stained waters that were flowing into the two bays in late September 2026, as well as the role that beavers have long played in the mythology and history of the region.

When the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image on September 27, 2026, the Moose, Nottaway, and Harricanaw rivers were carrying tea-colored water across the broad mudflats of Hannah and Rupert bays and mingling with the darker blue waters of James Bay.
The mudflats, the light brown areas along the shore, are a product of the shallow, sloping bathymetry in the southernmost part of James Bay.

European traders arrived in Rupert Bay as early as the 1660s to pursue the animals as well, leading to the establishment of several trading posts along the bay’s shores and the founding of the Hudson’s Bay Company to cultivate the fur trade, especially in beaver pelts.

For instance, one Cree myth about this area, recorded by the anthropologist Alanson Skinner , tells of a giant pursuing an enormous mythical beaver down the Nottaway River until the beaver escaped into Rupert Bay.

In an early example of a managed beaver preserve in Canada, the Hudson’s Bay Company worked with local Cree people in the 1830s and again a century later to set up Charlton Island as a place to raise beavers for later trapping.
